text: A 24-year-old man with a history of recurrent pulmonary infections presents with a groin abscess. Culture grows Staphylococcus aureus. Nitroblue tetrazolium testing reveals a lack of blue pigment formation in neutrophils.
lead: This patient is most likely deficient in which of the following enzymes?
objective: Chronic Granulomatous Disease is caused by NADPH oxidase deficiency, leading to inability to generate reactive oxygen species for bacterial killing.

text: A 73-year-old man undergoes coronary angiography via the femoral approach. He returns 2 days later with blue discoloration of his right toe and livedo reticularis. Serum creatinine is 2.8 mg/dL (preoperatively 1.0 mg/dL).
lead: Which of the following histopathologic findings would most likely be seen on biopsy of this patient's kidney?
options: Extensive necrosis of proximal tubular cells
objective: Atheroembolic renal disease follows invasive vascular procedures and presents with cholesterol clefts (cholesterol crystal emboli).

text: A 4-year-old boy has coarse facial features, clouded corneas, and restricted joint movement. Plasma lysosomal enzyme analysis shows elevated levels of enzymes that are normally sequestered in lysosomes.
lead: The primary defect in this patient involves which of the following processes?
objective: I-cell disease (mucolipidosis II) is caused by failure of the Golgi to phosphorylate mannose residues, preventing enzyme targeting to lysosomes.

text: A 28-year-old African American man develops dark urine and back pain 3 days after taking trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a UTI. Peripheral smear shows bite cells and Heinz bodies.
lead: Which of the following biochemical reactions is most likely impaired?
objective: G6PD deficiency impairs the pentose phosphate pathway, reducing NADPH and glutathione, leading to oxidative damage to RBCs.

text: A 32-year-old woman presents with diplopia and ptosis that worsens at the end of the day. Chest CT reveals an anterior mediastinal mass. Symptoms improve after administration of edrophonium.
lead: Antibodies in this patient are most likely directed against which of the following?
objective: Myasthenia gravis is caused by autoantibodies against postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction.

text: A 30-year-old man is evaluated for infertility. He has a history of recurrent sinusitis and bronchiectasis. The point of maximal cardiac impulse is palpable on the right side of the chest.
lead: Which of the following cellular structures is most likely defective?
objective: Kartagener syndrome (primary ciliary dyskinesia) is caused by dynein arm defects, leading to immotile cilia, situs inversus, and infertility.

text: A 15-year-old boy presents with jaundice and splenomegaly. Labs show a normocytic anemia with an elevated MCHC. An osmotic fragility test is positive.
lead: The defect in this patient most likely involves which of the following proteins?
objective: Hereditary spherocytosis is caused by defects in RBC membrane cytoskeleton proteins (ankyrin, spectrin, band 3), leading to spherocytes with increased osmotic fragility.

text: A 2-year-old girl has had 4 bone fractures after minor trauma. Physical exam shows blue sclerae and hearing loss. Her teeth appear grayish and translucent.
lead: This patient most likely has a defect in the synthesis of which protein?
objective: Osteogenesis imperfecta is caused by defects in type I collagen synthesis, leading to brittle bones, blue sclerae, and dentinogenesis imperfecta.

text: A researcher is studying glomerular filtration. After instilling a substance into the renal artery, the net filtration pressure increases from 10 mm Hg to 20 mm Hg without changing systemic blood pressure.
lead: Which of the following substances was most likely used in this experiment?
objective: Angiotensin II preferentially constricts the efferent arteriole, increasing glomerular hydrostatic pressure and GFR.

text: A 5-month-old boy has recurrent viral and fungal infections since birth. Chest x-ray shows an absent thymic shadow. Adenosine deaminase activity is absent in his erythrocytes.
lead: The accumulation of which metabolite is most likely toxic to this patient's lymphocytes?
objective: In SCID due to ADA deficiency, dATP accumulates and inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, preventing DNA synthesis in lymphocytes.

text: A 45-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease has bone pain. Labs show low calcium, high phosphate, and high PTH. Vitamin D levels are low.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely cause of her vitamin D deficiency?
options: Increased urinary loss of vitamin D
objective: In CKD, the failing kidney cannot perform 1-alpha-hydroxylation to convert 25-hydroxyvitamin D to active 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D.

text: A 3-month-old infant is brought in for large-volume watery diarrhea and failure to thrive. Jejunal biopsy shows absence of enteropeptidase activity in the brush border.
lead: Activity of which of the following enzymes is most directly impaired as a result?
objective: Enteropeptidase activates trypsinogen to trypsin. Trypsin then activates other pancreatic proenzymes including chymotrypsinogen.

text: A 22-year-old woman has recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, anxiety, and dark urine. During an episode, urine porphobilinogen levels are markedly elevated. She recently started oral contraceptives.
lead: Which enzyme is most likely deficient in this patient?
objective: Acute intermittent porphyria is caused by porphobilinogen deaminase deficiency. It presents with neurovisceral symptoms and is precipitated by drugs like OCPs.

text: A 6-year-old boy presents with recurrent bacterial infections. Flow cytometry shows absence of CD18 on leukocytes. Peripheral smear shows marked leukocytosis.
lead: Which of the following leukocyte functions is most likely impaired?
objective: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1 (LAD-1) is caused by CD18 deficiency, preventing leukocyte adhesion and migration to infection sites.

text: A newborn has ambiguous genitalia. Karyotype is 46,XX. Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone is markedly elevated. The infant has hyponatremia and hyperkalemia.
lead: Which enzyme is most likely deficient?
objective: 21-hydroxylase deficiency is the most common cause of congenital adrenal hyperplasia, causing virilization and salt-wasting in severe cases.

text: A 58-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder presents with confusion and ataxia. Examination shows horizontal nystagmus and ophthalmoplegia. His wife reports he has been eating poorly for weeks.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
objective: Wernicke encephalopathy requires immediate thiamine before glucose to prevent precipitation or worsening of symptoms.

text: A 67-year-old woman presents with sudden onset of severe headache described as the worst of her life. CT head without contrast is normal. She has mild neck stiffness.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Observation and repeat CT in 24 hours
objective: Negative CT does not rule out subarachnoid hemorrhage. LP is required to look for xanthochromia and RBCs if clinical suspicion is high.

text: A 45-year-old man with diabetes presents with left ear pain and purulent drainage for 2 weeks despite oral antibiotics. Exam shows granulation tissue in the external auditory canal. He has facial droop.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
objective: Malignant (necrotizing) otitis externa occurs in diabetics, caused by Pseudomonas, and can cause cranial nerve palsies (VII most common).

text: A 35-year-old woman presents with palpitations, weight loss, and heat intolerance. Labs show suppressed TSH and elevated free T4. Radioactive iodine uptake is very low.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
objective: Low radioactive iodine uptake in hyperthyroidism suggests thyroiditis (destruction releasing preformed hormone) or exogenous thyroid hormone.

text: A 62-year-old man with heart failure and atrial fibrillation is on warfarin. He develops acute left leg pain and pallor. The leg is cold and pulseless below the knee.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
options: CT angiography of the lower extremity
objective: Acute limb ischemia requires immediate heparin to prevent thrombus propagation while planning definitive revascularization.

text: A 28-year-old woman at 32 weeks gestation presents with severe headache, visual changes, and epigastric pain. BP is 168/110 mm Hg. Labs show platelets 85,000, AST 250 U/L, and LDH 800 U/L.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
objective: HELLP syndrome with severe features requires delivery regardless of gestational age after maternal stabilization with magnesium and antihypertensives.

text: A 55-year-old man with newly diagnosed lung cancer develops confusion and lethargy. Labs show sodium 118 mEq/L, serum osmolality 260 mOsm/kg, and urine osmolality 500 mOsm/kg. He appears euvolemic.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
objective: SIADH in a stable patient is initially treated with fluid restriction. Hypertonic saline is reserved for severe symptomatic hyponatremia.

text: A 42-year-old woman presents with 6 months of fatigue and joint pain. She has a malar rash and oral ulcers. Labs show positive ANA at 1:640 and positive anti-dsDNA antibodies. Urinalysis shows proteinuria.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
objective: Lupus nephritis requires renal biopsy to classify the disease and guide immunosuppressive therapy. Steroids are initiated while awaiting results.

text: A 70-year-old man with COPD presents with worsening dyspnea over 3 days. He has increased sputum production that is now purulent. Oxygen saturation is 88% on room air. Temperature is 37.8 C.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate antibiotic choice?
objective: COPD exacerbation with increased dyspnea, sputum, and purulence warrants antibiotics. Fluoroquinolones cover typical and atypical pathogens.

text: A 25-year-old man presents after a motor vehicle accident. He is alert but has neck pain. Cervical spine CT shows a type II odontoid fracture. He has no neurological deficits.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: Halo vest immobilization or surgical fixation
Soft cervical collar and follow-up imaging
objective: Type II odontoid fractures have high nonunion rates and typically require halo immobilization or surgical fixation.

text: A 60-year-old woman presents with progressive dysphagia to solids and liquids over 6 months. She also has regurgitation of undigested food. Barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus with a bird-beak appearance.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely finding on esophageal manometry?
options: Absent peristalsis with incomplete LES relaxation
objective: Achalasia shows absent peristalsis and incomplete LES relaxation on manometry due to loss of inhibitory ganglion cells.

text: A 48-year-old man with HIV (CD4 count 85 cells/microL) presents with headache and fever for 2 weeks. CSF shows elevated opening pressure, low glucose, elevated protein, and India ink positive.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
objective: Cryptococcal meningitis induction therapy requires amphotericin B plus flucytosine for at least 2 weeks before consolidation with fluconazole.

text: A 34-year-old woman presents with sudden onset of right flank pain radiating to the groin. She is writhing in pain. Urinalysis shows blood but no bacteria. CT shows a 4 mm ureteral stone.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
objective: Small ureteral stones (less than 5 mm) are likely to pass spontaneously. Medical expulsive therapy with alpha-blockers facilitates passage.

text: A 65-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on warfarin presents after a fall. He has a scalp laceration but no loss of consciousness. INR is 3.5. CT head shows a small subdural hematoma.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Prothrombin complex concentrate and IV vitamin K
Observation with repeat CT in 6 hours
objective: Intracranial hemorrhage on anticoagulation requires immediate reversal with PCC (faster than FFP) plus vitamin K for sustained effect.

text: A 55-year-old man with hypertension is found to have a 5.8 cm abdominal aortic aneurysm on screening ultrasound. He has no symptoms. Blood pressure is well controlled.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: Continued surveillance with ultrasound in 6 months
objective: AAA 5.5 cm or greater warrants elective repair due to increased rupture risk. CT angiography is needed for surgical planning.

text: A 72-year-old man with hypertension and diabetes is on Amlodipine 10mg daily. His BP remains 152/92 mmHg at follow-up. He has no side effects from current medication.
lead: Which of the following is the best next step in management?
objective: For uncontrolled hypertension on a CCB, adding an ACE inhibitor provides complementary mechanisms and is preferred in diabetics for renal protection.

text: A 45-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes on Metformin has HbA1c of 8.2%. BMI is 34. She is interested in medications that promote weight loss.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate medication to add?
objective: GLP-1 receptor agonists like semaglutide promote weight loss and have cardiovascular benefits, making them ideal for obese T2DM patients.

text: A 52-year-old man undergoes screening colonoscopy. Two tubular adenomas are found, measuring 0.8 cm and 1.2 cm. Both are completely removed.
lead: When should his next colonoscopy be performed?
objective: High-risk adenomas (any adenoma 1 cm or larger, or 3+ adenomas) require surveillance colonoscopy in 3 years.

text: A 35-year-old man with Major Depressive Disorder has been on sertraline 100mg for 3 weeks. He reports mild improvement but still has significant symptoms. No side effects.
lead: Which of the following is the best next step?
options: Continue current dose for 3 more weeks
objective: Antidepressants require 4 to 6 weeks for full effect. With partial response and no side effects, continue the current dose before adjusting.

text: A 28-year-old woman has frequent migraines (4 per month) lasting 12 to 24 hours each, causing her to miss work. She takes ibuprofen with partial relief.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate preventive therapy?
objective: Migraine prophylaxis is indicated for 4 or more headaches per month. First-line options include topiramate, propranolol, and amitriptyline.

text: A 72-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes, and prior stroke is diagnosed with atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc score is 5.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate stroke prophylaxis?
objective: CHA2DS2-VASc 2 or higher in men (3 or higher in women) requires oral anticoagulation. DOACs like apixaban are preferred over warfarin.

text: A 60-year-old man presents for preoperative evaluation before elective hip replacement. He has stable angina controlled with medications. His functional capacity is greater than 4 METs.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Proceed to surgery without further cardiac testing
objective: Patients with good functional capacity (greater than 4 METs) can proceed to intermediate-risk surgery without additional cardiac testing.

text: A 55-year-old man with recently diagnosed DVT is started on rivaroxaban. He asks about the duration of anticoagulation. The DVT was provoked by recent knee surgery.
lead: What is the recommended duration of anticoagulation?
objective: Provoked VTE (by surgery or other transient risk factor) requires 3 months of anticoagulation. Unprovoked VTE may warrant longer treatment.

text: An 82-year-old man hospitalized for pneumonia becomes agitated and confused at night. He is pulling at his IV lines and trying to get out of bed. He was oriented earlier today.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
objective: Delirium management prioritizes treating underlying causes and non-pharmacologic interventions. Antipsychotics are reserved for severe agitation.

text: A 4-year-old boy has fever and ear pain. Examination shows a bulging, erythematous tympanic membrane with decreased mobility. He has no drug allergies.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
objective: Acute otitis media in children 2 years and older with moderate symptoms is treated with high-dose amoxicillin as first-line therapy.

text: A 66-year-old woman asks about osteoporosis screening. She has no history of fractures and is not on any medications that affect bone. She went through menopause at age 52.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate recommendation?
options: Serum calcium and vitamin D levels only
objective: DEXA screening is recommended for all women 65 and older, or younger postmenopausal women with risk factors.

text: A 2-year-old boy has mild dehydration from viral gastroenteritis. He is able to drink fluids. Vital signs are stable.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
objective: Mild to moderate dehydration in children is treated with oral rehydration solution. IV fluids are reserved for severe dehydration or inability to tolerate oral intake.

text: A 45-year-old woman presents with a palpable thyroid nodule. TSH is normal. She has no symptoms of hyper or hypothyroidism and no family history of thyroid cancer.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
objective: Thyroid nodules with normal TSH are evaluated with ultrasound first to assess size, characteristics, and need for FNA biopsy.

text: A 35-year-old man presents with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back after a weekend of heavy drinking. Lipase is 1200 U/L. On day 3, he develops increasing abdominal distension and fever.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely cause of his clinical deterioration?
objective: Infected peripancreatic necrosis typically occurs after day 7 to 10, but infected fluid collections can occur earlier. Fever in acute pancreatitis suggests infection.

text: A 50-year-old woman with a mechanical mitral valve replacement presents with fever and new regurgitant murmur. Blood cultures grow Enterococcus faecalis. Echocardiogram shows vegetations.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate antibiotic regimen?
objective: Enterococcal endocarditis requires bactericidal synergy with ampicillin plus gentamicin (or ampicillin plus ceftriaxone for aminoglycoside-sparing).

text: A 25-year-old woman presents with palpitations and anxiety. She has lost 15 pounds despite increased appetite. Examination shows lid lag and a diffusely enlarged thyroid with bruit.
lead: Which of the following antibodies is most specific for her condition?
objective: Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSI) are specific for Graves disease and stimulate the TSH receptor, causing hyperthyroidism.

text: A 40-year-old man presents with chest pain that worsens with inspiration and improves when leaning forward. ECG shows diffuse ST elevation with PR depression. He had a viral illness last week.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
objective: Acute pericarditis is treated with NSAIDs (aspirin or ibuprofen) plus colchicine to reduce inflammation and prevent recurrence.

text: A 55-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis presents with confusion and asterixis. He has not had a bowel movement in 4 days. Ammonia level is elevated.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
objective: Hepatic encephalopathy is treated with lactulose to reduce ammonia absorption. Rifaximin can be added for recurrent episodes.

text: A 30-year-old woman presents with sudden onset of severe right lower quadrant pain. Her last menstrual period was 7 weeks ago. Urine pregnancy test is positive. She appears pale and BP is 85/50 mmHg.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
objective: Ruptured ectopic pregnancy with hemodynamic instability requires immediate surgical intervention. Imaging should not delay treatment.
